text:
Ottawa won this one on the scoresheet and on the ice, and the second claim is the more surprising one given how the middle of the game felt. Toronto held an edge in the quality of chances through two periods (about 2.17 expected goals to 1.94), got a tip-in from Auston Matthews 33 seconds into the second and a power-play backhand from Kirill Marchenko to lead 2-1. Then Michael Amadio tied it off a Thomas Chabot feed, and the third period belonged entirely to the Senators.

That period is the whole story. Ottawa generated 2.79 expected goals to Toronto's 0.99, and the simulated replays of every shot give the Senators a 74 percent chance of winning this game. Stephen Halliday's snap shot at 9:46, a 7 percent chance on its own, put them ahead for good. Chabot opened the scoring late in the first, then logged 27 minutes and finished with a goal and an assist, while Claude Giroux added two assists and was named second star.

The oddity is in the volume numbers. Toronto outattempted Ottawa 68 to 54, yet shots on goal were dead even at 29 apiece, and Ottawa blocked 19 shots to Toronto's 10. Toronto's attempts were quantity without much quality. Matthews took six shots and carried 0.93 expected goals of his own, but the Senators kept the best looks to the other end when it mattered.
